question: Organophosphate compounds (e.g., malathion, chlorpyrifos) are best classified as which type of poison by their origin?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Organophosphates are synthetic organic compounds derived from phosphoric acid; they are man-made carbon-containing chemicals classified under organic synthetic poisons in the Indian forensic taxonomy.
Incorrect. Animal poisons originate from living organisms — venoms (snake, scorpion, spider) and toxins from insects/marine organisms. Organophosphates are entirely synthetic.
Incorrect. Mineral poisons are inorganic compounds — heavy metals (arsenic, lead, mercury) and non-metallic inorganic salts. Organophosphates are carbon-based organic molecules.
Incorrect. Gaseous poisons are defined by their physical state at room temperature (CO, HCN, chlorine gas). Organophosphates are liquid or solid chemical agents, not gaseous.

overallFeedback.feedback: Organophosphates are organic synthetic poisons — man-made, carbon-containing, derived from phosphoric acid. Classification by origin: animal (venoms) | vegetable (plant alkaloids) | mineral (metals/inorganic) | synthetic organic (OP, carbamates, DDT).
Correct. Always classify a poison by BOTH its origin (animal/vegetable/mineral/synthetic) AND its action (corrosive/irritant/neurotropic/etc.) — the Indian FM taxonomy uses both axes simultaneously.
